name: Documentary Film and Video-MFA

rules.name: Production Core
rules.desc: In the production core, students are required to conceptualize and visualize their ideas in a series of writing and producing courses that focus on documentary story structure. These courses are taken in tandem with project-based production courses that provide training in the technical and conceptual aspects of cinematography, sound recording, editing, and sound design. Discussion of form and content is a signature component of the writing and production courses. The production core is complemented by a series of required film studies courses in documentary, elective courses in the history, aesthetics, ideology, and theory of all genres of moving image media, elective courses in studio art, and choice electives. All courses must be taken for a letter grade.

rules.name: Core Film Production Courses
rules.notes: Courses must be taken in sequence. Failing a course in the sequence may lead to dismissal from the program.

rules.name: Core Companion Film Production Courses
rules.notes:
Courses must be taken in one of following sequences:

• FILMPROD 410, FILMPROD 411, FILMPROD 413
or

• FILMPROD 411, FILMPROD 413, FILMPROD 410
Failing a course in the sequence may lead to dismissal from the program.

rules.name: GPA of 3.0 each quarter in degree courses
Research or Project Requirement
rules.desc:
In the program’s second year, each student produces a 15-20 minute documentary that constitutes the thesis project. In FILMPROD 405, students research and develop their project and write a proposal for submission.
Production takes place during winter break and/or during winter quarter(FILMPROD 406); post-production occurs in winter and spring quarters in FILMPROD 406 and FILMPROD 407.

gpa: Students must maintain a 3.0 grade point average in courses applicable to the degree each quarter.
grading: If a student receives a grade of B- or below in any of their core courses or electives, the student will be immediately notified both in person and in writing that they are not performing in a satisfactory manner and placed on academic probation. If, after an additional quarter, the student's work does not improve and they receive another B- or below in any of their courses, they may be dismissed from the program..
transferPolicy: All work for the degree must be completed in residence at Stanford.
reviewNotes: Every course must be letter graded. You take the seven core film production courses in sequence (FILMPROD 405, 406 and 407 also make up the thesis film), FILMEDIA 410 and 411, the three companion production courses, one Studio Art course (4 units), two Film and Media Studies courses (8 units) and one choice elective of at least 4 units, for 56 units. Your advisor checks the 3.0 GPA each quarter, and a B- or below in a core course or elective means academic probation. The companion courses FILMPROD 410, 411 and 413 may be taken in either of two orders, and all three are required either way.
